newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Chile aims to expand Caribbean trade.
newsitem.headline: Chile aims to expand Caribbean trade.

text.p: The Chilean government is launching a Chilean-Caribbean chamber of commerce to help open new markets in the region, the country's envoy to the area said Wednesday.
Adolfo Carafi, Chile's ambassador to the Caribbean, said the chamber would be headquartered in Kingston and inaugurated on Sept. 26.
Carafi is accredited to Jamaica, the Bahamas, Barbados, Guyana, St. Vincent, Antigua, and the 14-member Caribbean Community (CARICOM).
The chamber will be targeted at companies in the English-speaking Caribbean, and may be expanded to include the wider Caribbean at a later date.
Chile's total trade with the Caribbean stood at some US$32 million last year, in favor of the Caribbean. Carafi said a number of Caribbean products, like rum, possess good market potential in Chile.
Trinidad is Chile's largest single trade partner, exporting mostly petroleum products, followed by Jamaica. Jamaica's tourist industry is also attracting a growing number of Chilean tourists.

Officials said one of the chamber's main thrusts will be to attract Chilean investors into the region. Since Chile reformed its pension system in 1981, pension funds had attracted over US$20 billion by the end of 1994, and the funds are now looking overseas for investment opportunities.

Chile is now negotiating its entry into the North American Free Trade Agreement, as well as an agreement with Mercosur. Ambassador Carafi noted Chile could serve as the Caribbean's gateway into Mercosur, which groups Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay and Brazil.
